full_judgment: 24. The fundamental and basic presumption in the administration of the criminal law and justice delivery system is the innocence of the alleged accused till the charges are proved beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of clear, cogent, credible or unimpeachable evidence. In a criminal trial, the burden of proving the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts always rests on the prosecution and on the failure it cannot fall back upon the evidence adduced by the accused in support of his defence to rest its case solely thereon.
